verdict.rationale: Name.com documents self-serve credentials: developers issue development and production API tokens from Account Settings and authenticate with HTTP Basic Auth. Its docs also describe a sandbox that mirrors production and lets developers run integration tests without affecting real domains or incurring real charges. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that sandbox registrations work and are free.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get API credentials self-serve and test safely — a sandbox or test environment where registrations don't cost real money

citations.quote: Go to Account Settings → Security → API Tokens and issue both development and production tokens
The Core API uses **HTTP Basic Authentication** with your name.com API credentials.
a sandbox (testing) environment that mirrors production request/response shapes, so you can build and run automated integration tests without affecting real domains or incurring real charges.
